topic: LLM 정렬을 위한 선호 최적화: RLHF, DPO와 그 후속 방법
scope: Preference optimization for aligning large language models: from RLHF (learning a reward model from human preferences and optimizing it with PPO-style RL) to DPO and its successors, including direct, offline, reference-free, and online/RL-with-verifiable-reward variants. It stops at methods for post-training LLM alignment and does not cover pretraining or general-purpose RL.
paper_count_reason: The topic is broad, with six active lineages running from 2017 preference-based RL to 2025 GRPO and verifiable-reward work, so the survey covers 22 papers. That is enough to cover the founding works, the turning points (InstructGPT, DPO, GRPO) and the main successors in each lineage. Benchmarks, generic LLM reports, application papers and minor DPO variants are left out.

lineages.name: RLHF foundations and PPO-based pipelines
lineages.description: Learning reward models from human comparisons and optimizing them with PPO under a KL penalty, from Atari preferences to InstructGPT and Llama 2, including reward overoptimization.

lineages.name: AI feedback and scalable oversight
lineages.description: Replacing human preference labels with model-generated critiques and preferences (Constitutional AI, RLAIF).

lineages.name: Direct preference optimization (DPO and generalizations)
lineages.description: Closed-form reparameterization of the KL-regularized RLHF objective that trains directly on preference data, plus its theoretical generalizations and failure modes.

lineages.name: Reference-free and simplified objectives
lineages.description: Ranking and odds-ratio losses and length-normalized rewards that drop the reference model or the separate SFT stage.

lineages.name: Online, iterative and game-theoretic preference optimization
lineages.description: Fresh on-policy sampling, iterative DPO and Nash/self-play formulations that go beyond the Bradley-Terry reward model.

lineages.name: Critic-free RL and verifiable rewards
lineages.description: Lighter PPO replacements such as GRPO, applied with verifiable rewards to train reasoning models.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences
papers.authors: Paul Christiano, Jan Leike, Tom B. Brown et al.
papers.reason: Founding work that learns a Bradley-Terry reward model from pairwise trajectory preferences and optimizes it with deep RL.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
papers.authors: Daniel M. Ziegler, Nisan Stiennon, Jeffrey Wu et al.
papers.reason: First application of preference reward models plus PPO with a KL penalty to pretrained language models.

papers.title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
papers.authors: Nisan Stiennon, Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu et al.
papers.reason: Shows that RLHF at scale beats supervised baselines on summarization and establishes the SFT, reward model, PPO recipe.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.authors: Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu, Xu Jiang et al.
papers.reason: InstructGPT: the canonical three-stage RLHF pipeline that made the method mainstream for assistants.

papers.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.authors: Yuntao Bai, Andy Jones, Kamal Ndousse et al.
papers.reason: Anthropic HH-RLHF: helpful/harmless preference data, an iterated online mode and the HH dataset used by later direct methods.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
papers.authors: Leo Gao, John Schulman, Jacob Hilton
papers.reason: Quantifies reward model overoptimization (Goodhart's law), which motivates the KL regularization and the alternatives that followed.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Sandipan Kundu et al.
papers.reason: Constitutional AI replaces human harmlessness labels with AI critiques and preferences guided by written principles.

papers.title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears
papers.authors: Zheng Yuan, Hongyi Yuan, Chuanqi Tan et al.
papers.reason: RRHF: an early ranking-loss alternative to PPO that needs no RL, a precursor of the simplified objectives.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell et al.
papers.reason: DPO: derives a closed-form policy loss from the KL-regularized objective, removing the explicit reward model and the RL loop.

papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.authors: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin, Kevin Stone et al.
papers.reason: Llama 2-Chat documents an open, industrial RLHF recipe combining rejection sampling and PPO with separate safety and helpfulness reward models.

papers.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
papers.authors: Harrison Lee, Samrat Phatale, Hassan Mansoor et al.
papers.reason: Systematically shows that RLAIF can match RLHF, supporting AI feedback as a scalable labeling source.

papers.title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Preferences
papers.authors: Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Mark Rowland, Bilal Piot et al.
papers.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
papers.reason: The PsiPO framework explains DPO's overfitting under deterministic preferences and proposes IPO.

papers.title: Nash Learning from Human Feedback
papers.authors: Rémi Munos, Michal Valko, Daniele Calandriello et al.
papers.reason: Nash learning from human feedback replaces reward maximization with finding the Nash equilibrium of a preference model.

papers.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
papers.authors: Kawin Ethayarajh, Winnie Xu, Niklas Muennighoff et al.
papers.reason: KTO learns from unpaired desirable/undesirable signals via a prospect-theoretic utility, generalizing beyond pairwise data.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.authors: Zhihong Shao, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu et al.
papers.reason: Introduces GRPO, a critic-free PPO variant using group-relative advantages that became the standard for reasoning RL.

papers.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
papers.authors: Jiwoo Hong, Noah Lee, James Thorne
papers.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.reason: ORPO merges SFT and preference alignment through an odds-ratio penalty with no reference model.

papers.title: Human Alignment of Large Language Models through Online Preference Optimisation
papers.authors: Daniele Calandriello, Daniel Guo, Remi Munos et al.
papers.reason: Online IPO/DPO: shows that sampling fresh on-policy data closes the gap between offline direct methods and RLHF.

papers.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
papers.authors: Yue Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Huizhuo Yuan et al.
papers.reason: SPPO: a self-play algorithm that approximates the Nash policy and handles intransitive preferences, scaling to strong open models.

papers.title: RLHF Workflow: From Reward Modeling to Online RLHF
papers.authors: Hanze Dong, Wei Xiong, Bo Pang et al.
papers.reason: An open recipe for online iterative RLHF with iterative DPO, documenting its gains over offline training.

papers.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
papers.authors: Yu Meng, Mengzhou Xia, Danqi Chen
papers.reason: SimPO uses a length-normalized average log-probability reward plus a margin and drops the reference model, giving strong results.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
papers.authors: Rafael Rafailov, Yaswanth Chittepu, Ryan Park et al.
papers.reason: Shows that direct alignment algorithms also overoptimize, connecting DPO back to the reward hacking problem.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards: GRPO's Effective Loss, Dynamics, and Success Amplification
papers.authors: Youssef Mroueh
papers.reason: Analyzes GRPO under verifiable binary rewards as a weighted contrastive loss, linking it back to preference objectives.

excluded.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
excluded.reason: LoRA is a generic parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, not a preference optimization method.

excluded.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
excluded.reason: WebGPT is mainly an application of RLHF to browsing QA and adds no new method beyond InstructGPT's lineage.

excluded.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
excluded.reason: A survey of open problems; useful background but not a method.

excluded.title: Diffusion Model Alignment Using Direct Preference Optimization
excluded.reason: Applies DPO to diffusion models, which is outside LLM alignment.

excluded.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
excluded.reason: Safe RLHF is a constrained multi-objective variant, peripheral to the main preference optimization lineages.

excluded.title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
excluded.reason: Reward model ensembles are a minor mitigation; overoptimization is already covered by Gao et al.

excluded.title: Token-level Direct Preference Optimization
excluded.reason: Token-level DPO is a minor variant of DPO.

excluded.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
excluded.reason: PRO overlaps closely with RRHF as a ranking-loss method.

excluded.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
excluded.reason: Self-Refine is inference-time refinement, not preference training.

excluded.title: Sequence Level Training with Recurrent Neural Networks
excluded.reason: Sequence-level RL for NLP predates and sits outside preference-based alignment.
